intro: Make a photo to PDF under 100 KB in a few taps. Add the image or two, set the order, and the PDF lands below 100 KB without leaving your device.

faq.q: Can I convert a PNG or HEIC to a PDF under 100 KB?
faq.a: Yes. JPG, PNG, WebP and iPhone HEIC photos are all accepted.

faq.q: Can I add an existing PDF to the photos?
faq.a: Yes. Its pages are turned into images and inserted where you place the file.

faq.q: What if 100 KB is not enough?
faq.a: You are told the smallest size reached. Remove a page or choose a higher limit if your form allows it.

sections.h2: Where an image to PDF under 100 KB is needed
paras: Many state and university forms cap each document at 100 KB, for papers such as a domicile certificate, a gap-year affidavit or an income certificate. For NEET UG, whose address proof and category certificate must be PDFs of 50 to 300 KB, a 100 KB PDF is also a safe pick: comfortably above the floor and well under the top.

sections.h2: How many photos fit in 100 KB
paras: Two pages with clear text, three if the pages are plain. Each A4 page needs about 40 KB to keep normal print readable once it is scaled for a small file. With four or more pages, the tool will still produce a PDF under 100 KB, but every page gets smaller; check the preview before you rely on it.
Photos straight from a modern phone are 2 to 5 MB each, so the tool first caps them at 2000 pixels on the long side and then searches for the best JPEG quality that fits.

The PDF follows the list from top to bottom, so put page 1 first; for a two-sided document, front then back. A4 places each photo on an A4 sheet with margins, which looks like a proper document when the portal or an officer opens it. Original keeps each photo’s shape, which wastes nothing on borders and is better for small items.
Pick the size your form names, or open the JPG to PDF hub to type any maximum. Already have a PDF that is too big? Compress it instead.
